utterances.text: No. It's a straight road. It doesn't go towards the river. I apologise. May I say the following: The 27th of July Street, the Obala 27 Juli, 27th of July Street, then we get Ivana Krndelja Street, cuts across, which means that it is further away from the Miljacka, whereas the 27th of July Street is right by, alongside, the Miljacka River.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it was further away from the river than the Obala 27th July Street?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would seek your leave to ask some further questions of this witness. It may be that I could ask some questions that would throw some further light on what you have, I think, correctly identified as an issue. Therefore, I would seek the opportunity to ask those questions, with a view to clarifying the apparent discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then, of course, the Defence would have the opportunity to ask any additional questions. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. Mr. Ierace will put some questions to you on the same issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be shown Exhibit -- I think it's P3268, which comprises two photographs, and might the witness also retain the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Madam, please look at the two photographs, in particular, the one which has the "2" on it in a circle. Do you have that photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it please be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see on that photograph you have drawn the position of the barricades?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In other words, you have identified that intersection as the one where you and your daughter were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you notice that the photograph is looking up Ivana Krndelja Street towards, having regard to your evidence, the direction of the river?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivana Krndelja Street is a straight street. Number "1" indicates my movements, and that is Ivana Krndelja Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And is the street in photograph 2 also Ivana Krndelja Street?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ivana Krndelja Street is the street where I walked down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And where you were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This place, this part -- I don't know the upper part of the street, what the upper part of the street is called, but the street I moved along is Ivana Krndelja Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you have given evidence that, as you look at photograph 2, you crossed the street behind the barricades from right to left; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And moved on the left-hand side, walking straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see where you've placed the barricades in that photograph, photograph 2?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've told us that you crossed the street behind the barricades, and as you emerged from the protection of the barricades, you and your daughter were shot; correct?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now --

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. This is part of the pedestrian crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pedestrian lane.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In any event, as you look at that photograph and you look further away from the hill from where you were shot, do you agree that you cannot see the Miljacka River in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, please, look at the map and look at where you placed the red cross. Do you see that you have placed the red cross at the beginning of a bridge going over the river? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, having regard to the answers you just gave me to my early questions, do you agree that the cross marks a different position from the position in the photographs that you identified as where you were shot?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I say that the precision of the map and the photographs was not something I measured, but as I knew the image, I marked the spot, to the best of my recollections, the exact spot. Now, quite possibly, on the map, because of the scale of the map, there has been some slight discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is to say, the closeness of the Miljacka River and the actual spot I was in. But this is the exact spot and it is the right street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would you please take a blue marker, and first of all, would you look carefully at the map, and in particular, at Ivana Krndelja Street. And having looked at that street on the map, can you first tell me if you can identify the part of the street where indeed you were shot.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remembered, I did mark it exactly, to the best of my recollections.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Except, as you've already agreed, the spot you marked is at a bridge going over the river. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but precision -- the precision of the map -- perhaps there's just a little discrepancy between the map and the picture, but I did try and locate and mark the exact spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. No one's suggesting that you didn't do your best. Would you please look at photograph 1.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Look at photograph 1, please.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And do you see that on that photograph, the position where you were shot was very close to a T-intersection on Ivana Krndelja Street?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please look back at the map. Do you see the map shows only one street on Ivana Krndelja Street, which is a T-intersection, that is, with the stem of the "T" facing west?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the map to the left --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. I see several intersections in the shape of a "T" with the road, so the question seems to me to be very imprecise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm happy to rephrase it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, do you see that, having regard to the position of the river, that the view of Ivana Krndelja Street in photograph 1 is looking away from the river? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could I have -- could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and could we perhaps have the photo 1 on the ELMO at this moment so that we can see whatever the witness points at. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This was just precisely what I wanted to say, is that we did not have a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to your earlier evidence, the barricades that you have marked on photograph 1 are in Ivana Krndelja Street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In other words, one can view, in photograph 1, the end of Ivana Krndelja Street, that is, the intersection beyond the barricades that you marked?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to object, Mr. President. It is absolutely not certain that this photograph can show the end of the street, and this question is suggesting that there is -- that you can see the end of the street, and this is not acceptable for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it again, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see that to the right of the barricades and immediately before the barricades, there is a street going off to the right? I'll rephrase that again. I apologise. Do you see that just before the barricades, there is a street going off to the right?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In other words, the photograph shows a T intersection because there is not a street going off to the left?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please look at the map. Having regard to your earlier evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please put the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- are you able to identify that particular intersection on the map? And please take your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please find the road just indicated by Mr. Ierace as going to the right. But before doing so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What I would like is for us to be extremely precise. If there is no street coming from the other side, then there cannot be a T junction. It could be a letter L. So we would then have the same letters [as interpreted]. But there must be two streets going off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber does not agree with your conclusion. Mrs. Taric, Mr. Ierace just indicated a road on picture 1 going to the right. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please indicate on the map where that road is. Take your time and find it. You don't have to hurry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can recall, I'll show it to you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please indicate that on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this is -- if this is the answer, then I'll show you the direction that I was walking in. Map is one thing, but here we can see an intersection on the map where several streets are crossing. And on the photograph is the actual spot where there is no intersection of these streets. In fact, the photographs are slightly further away from the Miljacka River. Logically speaking, it means that the photograph and the map are not quite on the same location because the photographs are from the scene of the incident, and this is perhaps what is bringing confusion because there is no intersection as it is on the map. But if I'm saying the exact direction of my movement, of the direction that I was walking in, perhaps that could clear up the map and the photograph. Yes, it happened in Ivana Krndelja Street, the spot that I marked with a cross. I may have possibly not have been totally precise about where I marked the cross on the map. The photographs are correct, because of the scale of the map, but I will mark it again. I will show it again. From Hrasno, I was going along the street which is in the other direction, not the direction I was walking in, the Brace Ribar Street. So I arrived -- this is the beginning, not the end, of Ivana Krndelja Street. Ivana Krndelja continues on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't seek to ask any more questions. I rely on the last...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, any additional questions on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm sorry, Mr. President, but we are going to have to have the 360-degree photograph just to clarify these things. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... on the ELMO under "Computer Evidence." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, madam, you just said that the photographs 1 and 2 that you were just shown did not correspond to the indications, the markings, that you've put on the map in relation to the incident. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not right. The photographs are the spot. They are the spot where the incident happened. So this is just a slightly smaller scale than the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just -- Mrs. Taric, so what you tell us is that whenever there would be any imprecision in the marking of the red "X," at least the place indicated on the photographs is the exact place of where the incident took place. That's what you have told us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to see the 360-degrees photograph, Mr. President, if that is possible. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on the screen. If you push the right button, it's under "Computer Evidence." I see -- you found it, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [No Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have got it when I push the button "Computer Evidence."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure we have the same thing. But I have it on the other screen, but it's fine. Thank you. Thank you very much. Yes, we have it now. Witness, so that we can locate the spot, I would like to ask the technicians to zoom slightly out, because I believe that there were some -- to the right, please. No, not the back zoom, in the other direction, please, zooming in. And then slightly to the right because I believe that there was a traffic sign. See if you can go -- zoom in a little bit, please. A little bit further. A little bit further until the actual sign, road sign, is visible. I believe this is a traffic sign. Could we locate... I don't know if we have the same thing on our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there it is again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now try and focus on this road sign, please, which we can see in front of us. Yes, a little bit further so that we can actually -- so it becomes legible. If it's not possible, then obviously not. I think this is a road sign. Could we go -- could we zoom in. Could we go a bit further. I don't know whether this is possible technically, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the technician can hear us, so could you please zoom in as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, please. Could we focus on the traffic sign unless it is not legible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be zoomed in even more. Yes. Yes. I don't know whether it becomes any better legible, but what I see is a triangle and a circle on the traffic sign. It doesn't bring me any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I don't think that we will be able to read what is on the sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Simply, Witness, if we can go back to the image that we had on our screens before, which was showing the street when it was at the beginning of this presentation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, for the technical booth, is it possible to have the same image that we had at the very beginning of this presentation of this image. No, that wasn't it. Here it is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, we now know which one is the main street. Just so that we make absolutely sure of the situation, could you tell us the name of the area, the mountainous area, that we see in the background of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean down there?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm talking about the centre, the middle of the screen. You can see some elevations, some hills in the background perspective of the photograph. What is it?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, could it be said that the camera -- that the image that was visible on the screen at the time that Mr. Piletta-Zanin asked his question depicted the street Ivana Krndelja - and I apologise for my pronunciation - looking approximately north up that street. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you agree that it is north? Because it's...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have a lot of trouble finding my way around in everyday life. But when I look at the 360-degree photograph, then it's even worse. But if the witness is not certain about the names of the areas around, I'm not sure myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the answer is that you do not agree that it was north, since you are not able to orient yourself. Then for the record, the image at that time shows an apartment block on the left with some green interrupted striping. It shows a high-storey -- approximately 12-, 13-storey apartment block on the right-hand side with red striping on it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 12. 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in the background, we see some elevations. And I do understand that Judge Nieto-Navia has another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes, just to clarify this problem. Using the 360-degrees photograph, we see the traffic lights.

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we can see it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... on that street, the one close in there?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Straight, the street road, I don't know what it is called. But the street to the left is Ivana Krndelja Street. By the traffic lights to the left, that's Ivana Krndelja Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: You don't know the name of the other crossing street?

utterances.speaker: NAFA TARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This, then, concludes your examination as a witness. To start, I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, which is a very long distance for you, and you were in an environment -- I see that there's some manipulation on the screen at this moment not ordered by me or by anyone else. So I would urge whoever is at the technical booth not to show any images on any screen unless it has been ordered by the Trial Chamber or has been agreed upon by the Trial Chamber to have it asked by one of the parties. So I'm sorry for this interruption. I thank you very much for having come to The Hague. It must have been a rather strange environment for you. You well understand that, for all the decisions we'll have to take, it's of vital importance that we get the information from those who have been at the places and at the times where Mr. Galic has been charged with offences. Thank you very much for coming. I wish you a safe trip home. And please, Mr. Usher, would you then guide Mrs. Taric out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to decide on the documents that have been tendered into evidence. Apart from, I would say, the more or less routine documents, as far as the previous statement of the witness has been tendered into evidence, both in the English version and the B/C/S version, the Chamber will admit into evidence those pages where the text can be found as far as the army commander is concerned. Since the Registry has not been provided yet with copies, would you please, during the next break, provide copies of these particular pages which Madam Registrar will then receive the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D35 for the statement in English, and D35.1 for the B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I understand the limited purpose for which this document is being admitted, but the Prosecution would ask that, in lieu of the sole page, that the entire document, which is only three pages - a cover page, the page in question, and the final page -

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: - that that entire document be admitted rather than simply part of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it has been -- is there any specific reason why you want to have any extra -- I mean, the issue was about the military commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, I understand that, Mr. President. It's simply for issues of completeness rather than simply admitting part of a statement but not the entire statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a position different from the position taken before by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll withdraw the objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, Madam Registrar, I think let's, then, resume at the Prosecution exhibits. That would be, I think, the video, and 360-degree photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video will be P3280I; the 360-degree photograph, P3279H; the set of two photographs, P3268; and the map, P3105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then I think we have another Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. The report, two-page, D36.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And of course also, Mr. President, there were the medical records which have been previously admitted but which pertain to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Also, just to answer a previous query of the Trial Chamber: I sent an e-mail to the investigator with respect to audio and/or videotapes taken of the interviews with this witness, and I've received a message back that confirmed what I previously stated, that is, there are no existing -- or no tape recordings of those statements were actually made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your information. I think we are then at a point where the Prosecution could call its next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will be taking that witness. It is Mensur Jusic. It relates to -- the evidence relates to incident number 24 on the first schedule of the indictment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, first of all, welcome into this courtroom far away from your home. We are quite grateful that you have come to The Hague. If you are examined as a witness -- you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a little louder, please. If the interpretation channel could be a little louder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that better, Mr. Jusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I spoke a few words of welcome to you, especially for coming to The Hague. You'll be examined as a witness in this courtroom, and the Rules require you to make a solemn declaration. The text of that declaration will be given to you by the usher, and would you then -- I would then invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated. If you would please come a bit closer, perhaps, to the microphones so that everyone can hear you well. You will first be examined by Mr. Ierace, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please tell the Trial Chamber your full name.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: My name is Mensur Jusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: 7th of July, 1957.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, before -- I withdraw that. In 1992, were you living in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was your occupation in early 1992?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I worked for Sipad company, which was engaged in the production and sale of furniture around the world, and I was engaged in the department which dealt with the export of furniture to Scandinavian countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And indeed, do you have some -- a degree of working knowledge of English, the English language?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I could use English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. During the armed conflict in Sarajevo, at one stage were you a member of the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Until what time?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Until the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you do after you left the army?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: In early January 1994, I was hired by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that is where I still work.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did that involve you working within the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During 1994, were you living within the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you travelled between your home and your workplace, did you sometimes walk?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you sometimes use public transport?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: At the time, when there would be a truce signed for the city of Sarajevo, then the trams would start working, and during such periods of time, I used the tram as a means of transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you have any concerns as to your personal safety in choosing to travel by tram?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was always a certain unease, certain misgivings, certain apprehension, fear, that something could happen on my way to my place of work and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why, having regard to that concern, did you sometimes choose to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. travel by tram rather than, say, walk?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: The danger involved in going to work -- well, it is difficult to really say what was -- what presented a bigger danger, whether walking to work or taking a tram. Possibly I thought that if a truce had been agreed, a ceasefire had been agreed, and then a tram, which is a means of public transportation, that it would not be targeted. So in that sense, I thought that perhaps the danger was lesser, and of course it took you less time and you were less exposed; you spent less time in an open space if you used some means of transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During the armed conflict, were there any occasions when, whilst you were on a tram in Sarajevo, shots were fired at the tram?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Once I was an eyewitness to the fire opened on a tram, when I was lightly wounded myself, and I also eyewitnessed an attack on a tram, not the tram that I was in but a tram which was somewhere near my tram, coming from the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will first ask you some questions about the incident when you were wounded. What date was that?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to give you the exact date, but it could have been late spring/early summer, so June, perhaps June, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What time of day was it, approximately, when you got on the tram?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I had finished my work. I finished doing what I was doing sometime around 1700 and I boarded the tram which was nearest to my workplace, and the incident then could have happened some ten minutes before or after 5.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were you going when you got on the tram?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I was on my way home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What clothes were you wearing?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I had a pair of jeans on and a T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What road were you on when you caught the tram?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I boarded the tram across the building of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that is Marsal Tito Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is Marsal Tito Street a street that runs approximately parallel to the Miljacka River, in an east-west direction?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the tram you boarded travel from east to west or from west to east?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: It was going from east to west, that is, from the centre of the town towards Ilidza, and that is the east-west direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately how many people -- I withdraw that. You've told us that whilst you were on that tram, the tram was shot at. At the time that there was shooting, whereabouts on the tram were you?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I was -- it is an articulated tram, and I was in the first part, in the first carriage, at the rear door of the first carriage.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You say that it was an articulated tram. Did it have two or more than two components?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately how long was it after you boarded the tram that there was shooting?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Six, seven to maybe ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately how many people were there on the tram at the time of the shooting?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: There were not many passengers. I'd say 15 to 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've told us that you were in the first carriage at the rear door. At the time of the shooting, were you seated or standing?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I was standing, yes, right at the door, not on this stair down. I was on the platform, but I was standing right next to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you could just imagine being in the tram and facing the direction in which the tram was travelling, were you to the left of the carriage or the right of the carriage or somewhere in the middle?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I was standing, if I understand your question, I was -- if we look at how the tram moves, then I was on the right-hand side of the tram in the direction of the movement of the tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please tell the Trial Chamber, when you say there was shooting, exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I felt a powerful impact of a bullet against the tram, that is, one shot, something like a small explosion. I mean less intensive explosion. And I noticed right behind me a person who was with a little boy, and I saw blood. At that moment, I could not see which one of the two of them was bleeding, but there was quite a lot of blood. After that, I felt that I had also been hit in the shin of my right leg. And I noticed a young woman, who was standing to my right, about a metre away from me, not further than that, that she was also bleeding from her arm. Naturally, the situation was quite dramatic. The passengers reacted in a very natural manner. We all went down to the floor in the tram. There were no further shots. There was this one shot. And what I can say, too, is that I smelled the gun powder in the tram. The tram continued moving. It did not come to a halt. And for another kilometre when it reached a stop, a stop called Pofalici. That was my stop, actually because I lived there. And it stopped at a place which is screened by a school, that is, there is a school there and a church. So that that part of where the tram came to a stop, it was screened off by these two buildings from the positions of the Serb army on Grbavica. And I simply had enough wits about me to try to see the exact place where the tram had been hit, and I observed that bullet - I do not know what kind of a weapon it was fired from - but it had hit that tram. If we were talking the direction of the movement of the tram, that bullet hit the left side of that tram and some 10 centimetres beneath the window in the rear part of the first carriage of that tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, I take you back to the time of the shooting. You told us that you were standing near the rear door of the first carriage, and that placed you on the right side of the tram. Which way were you facing at the time of the shot?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I had my back to the direction from which the bullet came. I had my back to whatever place that bullet came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you said that there was a woman to your right, about a metre away, who was bleeding from her arm, I take it she was a metre further back down the tram, a metre further away from the front of the tram. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that --

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But if I may say, she was not a woman. I think she was quite young, that is, a young woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said there was a person with a young child. What was the sex of that person who had the child?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: That person was a female, that is, of female sex, and the child was of the male sex.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately how old was the child, if you are able to recollect that?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: It was a very small child; two, three years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness be shown an exhibit. Excuse me. Perhaps Exhibit Number P3110.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, did you make a statement with the assistance of an investigator from the Prosecutor's office at the Tribunal on the 13th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time that you made that statement, did you make the diagram which is to your right at the moment on the ELMO in order to better explain the positions of various people in the tram at the time that the shot was fired?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please explain the relevance of the number "1" which you placed in a circle in red ink on the diagram.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Number "1" indicates the place where I was standing in the tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does the arrow indicate the direction in which the tram was travelling?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: No. This arrow indicates the direction -- or rather the place where the tram was hit by the bullet. That is the spot -- the place of the impact, if you mean this side here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise for that. I think there are two arrows on the diagram. You have just --

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Now I see this other arrow. Yes. It was not on the screen at the time when I looked at it first. Now I can see there are two arrows.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And does the arrow - that is, the black arrow - indicate the direction in which the tram was travelling? And by "black arrow," I mean the one to the left of the diagram as it appears on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, if you look on the ELMO, you will see the colours better than you see on the screen. The usher will explain to you where it is. If you look to the right on this machine, that's the original so you can --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- better see the colours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The arrow which is dark and which is parallel to the tram, this arrow here, is indicating - excuse me - is indicating the direction in which the tram was travelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, can you please indicate where the driver was seated. That is, the driver of the tram.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Well, the driver was sitting in his seat, which is at the very front of the tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think on the diagram you have placed a symbol to indicate the position of the driver. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Have you also drawn some lines to indicate where the two carriages joined? And if so, could you please indicate those. Could you please point to those lines.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's this place here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You indicated a position halfway, approximately, along the length of the train -- the tram. Have you also indicated four doors on the tram?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please point to those, one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: This is in the front part of the tram. There are two doors. This is the first one. This one is the second. And in the latter part of the tram, there are, once again, two doors, here and here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I take you back to the numbers that you have placed in red ink on the drawing. What does the number "2" signify?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Number "2" signifies the place where the young woman was standing, about which I had told you had been wounded in the arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the number "3"?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: And position "3" is the place where the lady was sitting, and next to her, her little son.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you said earlier that the red arrow indicates the direction of the bullet. Does it also indicate the point at which the bullet entered the tram, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is pointing at the place of impact. There are the windows, and some ten centimetres underneath these windows, it hit the plate or -- I don't know what the tram is made of. But at any rate, it hit this metal plate of which the tram is made of.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that at the time that the bullet hit, you heard an explosion and you smelled gunpowder. Had you previously had any experience of impacting bullets being accompanied by the smell of gunpowder?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: No, I did not have any experience with such a bullet, with this small -- I mean, something small -- well, I don't know. What is a small explosive device? I don't really know what that is, but I've never had experience with such a small explosive device before. That was the experience, for instance, I gained from rather large shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that the woman who was accompanied by the child was covered in blood. At any point were you able to determine whether either or both of them were injured as a result of this incident?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I never communicated with these people until I came to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you able to form an opinion as to whether the bullet remained intact or not after it entered the carriage?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, it's just two minutes past 12.30. If you'd find a suitable moment to interrupt your examination so that we can have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It happens that that is a convenient time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll then adjourn until 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, I do apologise for starting late, but there were good reasons, in relation with this trial, that kept us out of the courtroom for a couple of extra minutes. Mr. Ierace, you were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. An update on tomorrow morning. I propose to call Zoran Lesic following the completion of this witness's evidence. I anticipate he will still be cross-examined -- still be in cross-examination by the end of today's proceedings. The statement prepared by Zoran Lesic is nine pages in length. The English version was disclosed to the Defence on the 26th of November, 2001, the B/C/S version on the 17th of January, 2002. Much of the nine-page statement is highly technical in nature. I propose that, unusually, in relation to this witness, I tender his statement. That will, of course, also save a lot of time in relation to his examination-in-chief. If this course is acceptable to the Trial Chamber, I could have made available to the Trial Chamber this afternoon copies of his statement so that they could be read before he gives his evidence. I anticipate that evidence-in-chief beyond the contents of his statement would be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, any observations, apart from the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. time of calling the witness, also on the procedure suggested by Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for giving me the floor, Mr. President. I should like to ask the Prosecution to give us a copy of the document for us to be able to check through it. As for the timing, I know that it will be brief -- that the time is brief, and I don't know whether we'll be able to prepare ourselves by tomorrow, but we'll do our best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think I'd like to hear your opinion about where usually prior statements are not admitted into evidence, it is the suggestion that this would be different as far as Mr. Lesic is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that would be acceptable, Mr. President, if that was what you were referring to. I don't think that is acceptable. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please give the reasons why it would not be acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I admit that I don't hold in my head the whole of the document or anything that would help me refresh my memory. So I would like to see what the document is, what it contains before it is tendered and admitted into evidence. That is the least that can be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you still want to consider your position as far as the admission of evidence is concerned; and not having the content clearly in your mind at this moment, you would rather not take any decisive position. In these circumstances, I think this Chamber will deliberate this afternoon on whether tomorrow would be a good time to hear Mr. Lesic and, at the same time, we'll then hear from the Defence as soon as possible, whenever possible, even this afternoon, on whether rereading the text of the prior statement of Mr. Lesic would lead to any final conclusions as to the acceptance of the procedure suggested by Mr. Ierace. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the spirit of accommodating the Defence, an alternative course would be for the Prosecution to call Mr. Lesic early next week. I note that we are not sitting on Friday. That would give the Defence some three days, at least, to familiarise themselves with the statement's contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please communicate your position this afternoon to the senior legal officer. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we'll hear from the Defence this afternoon, and we'll see tomorrow how we proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: After having conferred again with my colleagues, the Chamber is of the opinion that the examination of Mr. Lesic could take place better in the beginning of next week instead of tomorrow. Since I do understand there's no problem in calling him, would you please keep that in mind in the order of calling your witnesses. Mr. Ierace, I think we could continue the examination-in-chief of the witness Jusic. Mr. Usher, could you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: THE COURT: Mr. Jusic, my apologies for not addressing you right away. I'm doing some technical things. The examination by Mr. Ierace will now continue. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, what was the time, approximately, that the tram was shot?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: As I said earlier on, approximately 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the weather at that time, the state of the weather?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: The weather was nice. It was sunny. It was daylight. It was a calm summer afternoon. A summer atmosphere prevailed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the nature of the road at the time the tram was shot? And by that, I mean was the tram at that point travelling across a part of Marsal Tito Street which had no intersection at all, or was there an intersection, or what?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: From the point that I boarded the tram, the tram passed one intersection, one crossroads. And the incident I'm testifying about took place at the next largest intersection, the biggest crossroads in the city of Sarajevo, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What roads comprise that intersection? What are the names of the roads?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: The street which cuts across vertically across the path the tram was taking is called Trscanska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At that point, and having regard to your evidence that the bullet entered the left side of the tram, was any part of the other side of the confrontation line in view?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At that time, that is, in June of 1994, were there confrontation lines around Sarajevo separating the opposing armies?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was the side of the confrontation line -- withdraw that. Was one side of the confrontation line occupied or at least defended by the forces of the Bosnian government army?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was one side of the confrontation line defended by forces of the Bosnian government army?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was the other side defended by the forces of the Bosnian Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I don't want to enter into the terms you used, which army as referring to the armies, but yes, it was defended.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What army did you understand was on the other side of the confrontation line, that is, the side other than the Bosnian government army side?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I consider that they were members or parts of the forces of the former Yugoslav People's Army, and part of the Serb people armed by that army and equipping them with the military materiel and equipment that belonged to the army of the former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you form an opinion as to the source of fire that hit the tram?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Could you say that again, please. Could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you arrive at a personal opinion as to where the bullet came from?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: The bullet could have come from the positions or parts of Sarajevo which are called the Jewish cemetery, the Jewish cemetery area, or it might have been another area surrounding the Jewish cemetery on the slopes of a mountain which is called Trebevic. So from that general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From the part of the tram line where the bullet entered the tram, was it possible to see those two areas?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On what side of the confrontation line at that time was that part of the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Roughly in the same direction frontally, if I can put it that way. More or less frontal, that was the position of the Jewish cemetery with respect to the tram, or thereabouts. Slightly more diagonally, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was the Jewish cemetery area at that time under the control of the Serb forces or the Bosnian government forces?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I wasn't in the area myself during the war, not actually in that area. But according to the information I have, that is the area in which the forces of the army were located, that is, to say the military forces which perpetrated the aggression on the town, surrounded the town and asserted the aggression on the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At that time, were the parts of Trebevic that you referred to also under their control or under the control of the Bosnian government armed forces?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Part of the defence towards Trebevic, the lower zone, was under the control of the forces of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, whereas the upper slopes, the upper reaches, apart from the lower area, which was the Jewish cemetery area, was under the control of the forces which had surrounded the town of Sarajevo and those which shelled Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which forces controlled that part of the lower area which included the Jewish cemetery area at that time, as you understood it?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that it could have been the forces of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time in that area. Quite possibly, if I am looking in the direction that the tram was moving, they might have been a little more towards the east, bearing in mind the configuration of the terrain, the houses, their height. There is a bypass road, a road which was specifically constructed for trucks to be able to exit the city, and it is above that road that the Jewish cemetery is located. Now, I'm not a military strategist so I can't say for sure. I don't know the positions exactly but I don't think it was possible that those forces were directly below positioned there, that is to say, the forces of the Bosnian government.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time that the tram received the shot, were there any military vehicles in the area?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there anyone on the tram at that time that you saw carrying a weapon?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: No, not then or at any time did I see any uniformed persons in the tram or persons bearing arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that when the tram finally pulled up at, as it happens, your stop, you got off the tram. What did the other people on the tram do at that time?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Some of the passengers got off at the same stop, and I assume that some passengers -- it's difficult for me to answer, to say, because they were split-second moments, and you don't pay much attention to things like that. But I did notice where the bullet entered. I looked around the tram, went round to see, and saw the entrance hole made by the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the tram proceed on past your stop at that point? In other words, did you see the tram move on?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. The tram moved on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you seek any treatment for your injury?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Nearby there was an emergency infirmary, and I went to them for help.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say "an emergency infirmary," do you know who operated that?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: The medical staff belonging to the emergency department, that is to say, people who were trained medical personnel, and there were also some civilians who had been trained medically and were part of the emergency first-aid service.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've mentioned that there was a second incident involving a tram that you witnessed. When was that?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: That was also sometime in the spring of 1994, or perhaps -- not much time went by between those two events. They were quite close to each other. Whether it was June or July, I can't be sure, but they followed on in rapid succession.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And whenever it was, I think you said that it involved -- I withdraw that. Whereabouts were you at the relevant time?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I was -- the tram I was riding in from town, after I had finished my work, at the end of the working day, stopped at the Pofalici stop. I got off the tram, and at that particular point, when I stepped down from the tram, you could hear a terrible burst of gunfire, and I heard shattering and the sound of bullets hitting metal and ricocheting and hitting the asphalt, and I automatically ran across the road to take cover by the building opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you able to determine, having regard to the sound, the general direction from which the gunfire had come?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: The gunfire had come from the direction of Grbavica, across the bridge, the Brotherhood and Unity Bridge. That's what the name of the bridge was at that time, the Bratstva-Jedinstva, Brotherhood and Unity Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which forces occupied Grbavica at that time?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: The forces that occupied the city of Sarajevo and which attacked the city of Sarajevo and shelled the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean by that the Serb forces, if I could call them that?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, what is the -- first of all, on what street was that tram stop, Pofalici?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: At the time, the name of the street was Vojvode Putnika Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was the stop at an intersection, or not?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: The stop was located just after the intersection, as you crossed over, just after the level crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What other streets formed that intersection?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: The street and the bridge were called Bratstva-Jedinstva. It was Bratstva-Jedinstva Square and Bratstva-Jedinstva Bridge, and the street that cuts across that street from the direction of the city was called, at the time, Vojvode Putnika Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recall what the state of light was at the time you heard the gunfire? In other words, was it night, was it day, or was it somewhere in between?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: It was somewhere in between. It wasn't quite dark yet. Dusk, twilight. Not day either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, having heard the burst of fire, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I had got off the tram I was in and I ran towards the building that was opposite the street. I crossed the street, then there was a grassy patch, and then there was this building which was some 50 metres away from the bus stop. On my way to the building, I saw a girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please take your time. How old was the girl, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Nine, ten years old, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would just need some time to come at ease, please tell me, Mr. Jusic. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think I'll be able to continue. I can go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever you think you're not able to continue, please let me know. And I'll ask, then, Mr. Ierace to continue the examination. Please, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right. I can continue. The girl was 9 or 10 years old and I saw her crawling along the street. I took her up in my arms and took her through this passageway between the building in front of us, and she was wounded. I took her through that passageway, carried her through. And we found a car somehow. I don't know whose the car was or which car it was, but there just happened to be a car. And the first-aid station was only 300 metres away, so I asked the driver to take the little girl to the emergency station, because she had been wounded, and I never knew what happened to her after that. I never had any contact with that little girl again. I don't know what happened to her or what became of her, how seriously wounded she was, whether she was that seriously wounded or not. I just don't know. But the car took the little girl to the emergency station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the -- from the time that you were pulling up to that tram stop until the time you left it, did you notice, first of all, anyone wearing a military uniform in the area?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice anyone carrying any weapons?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you hear or see anyone returning fire from around that area?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice any other trams in the area?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: The next day I was in contact with some other eyewitnesses of that event, and I realised then that the shooting was targeting a tram coming from the opposite direction that I was going in. There was another tram which crossed my tram.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: And what I learnt from the people who were there on the spot -- it was this other tram that was being fired at, not the tram I was actually in. Now, what happened to that tram, what the consequences of that shooting were, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you see any other adult in the vicinity of the girl at the time that you first saw her? Apart from yourself, of course.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember what clothing she was wearing?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: She was wearing some children's -- light children's clothing. As I said, it was summertime or spring, warm weather. I don't remember the details of what she was wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Apart from it being warm, do you remember anything else about the weather, such as whether it was raining or fine?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: It wasn't raining. It was a clear day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you also able to give evidence about another incident involving a group of people running across a street, during which someone was shot?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did that incident take place?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Well, this could have been early autumn, September, perhaps the latter part of September, in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, having regard to the indictment period, I don't propose to ask any questions about that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you also able to give evidence about an incident that you witnessed near the railway station in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did that incident take place?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to give you the exact time when that happened, the exact date. I can connect this incident to the reason why I was there at that place at all, so I can relate this to the time in early spring 1993. So it could have been February or March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was it possible it was 1994, that is, early spring 1994?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I remember that in the first statement that I gave, I mentioned February 1994, but later when I thought about it, I believe that the time when the incident happened was actually one year earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, on that occasion, where were you when there was some shooting? In other words, when you heard shooting.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I was in the area of the railway station, of the Sarajevo railway station, the main railway station in Sarajevo. More precisely, at the area where people get out of the station where carriages are parked or engines are parked that are not used, although, of course, the railway traffic -- transport in Sarajevo had stopped some time before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness be shown Exhibit P3112. That is the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Usher, would you give the map to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, at the time that you made your first statement, did you also place some markings on a map?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the map that is before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you do that on the 13th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you have that map, or at least a colour photocopy of it, in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see on that map Brodska Street?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Brodska, Brodska Street, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us that you were in the area of the railway station --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, there was another map that you provided the Registry with. I don't know whether you need that at a later stage, but... It creates confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In any event, Mr. President, I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could perhaps the map be placed on the ELMO so that we can be certain that the right map is...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Mr. President, the ELMO does not do a very good job with colours. I'd be grateful if I could see the map very briefly. The witness has the map that I intended him to have, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, did you mark on that map with a circle around a number where you were at the time that you heard shooting?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Indeed, did you place the number "1" inside the circle to indicate your position?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Will you tell us what you heard and what you saw when you were in that position?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I did not hear anything, but I saw a man in Brodska Street, and he fell. He just crumpled to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you hear anything at around that time, either immediately before you saw him or after, that is, before or after you saw him crumple and fall?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: The only thing I saw was that this man was obviously hit by a bullet, and he just fell. And I saw two or three people that approached him, and they pulled him away from the spot where he was shot in order to get him some protection and themselves some cover. And the way it happened, the spot was still being targeted, so it was not possible to approach the place. There was a vehicle nearby, a car that wanted to get to the spot and take the wounded, possibly transport the person to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How do you know that the position was still being targeted?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: This could be seen -- I could see -- I could see it on the asphalt. I could see the shooting. It was possible to see this. I could also see it by the reactions of the people that were surrounding the wounded man. This was at a distance for me of about 60, 70, possibly a hundred metres. 50 maybe. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, when you say you could see it on the asphalt, could you tell us what it is exactly you saw on the asphalt?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Well, you know, when a bullet hits the asphalt, there is a little bit of dust that goes up in the air. Or it was possible to see it on the grass from the pavement. It was possible to see that there was fire being opened in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was the man who fell to the ground in a uniform of any description?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was he carrying a weapon that you could see?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: No, I did not see that he was wearing a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were any of the two or three people that approached him and pulled him away wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I don't think they did have anything. I think they were also civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were any of them carrying a weapon that you could see?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I did not see any weapons. I did not see that they were carrying any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there anything about any of them that suggested to you that they were members of a military force?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you able to determine the direction of the fire that you observed? In other words, from which direction it came?

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: I can conclude from a previous experience I had on that same spot, and I was accompanying my wife's sister at the time, and we lost her as well in the spring of -- about two months later. What I mean is two months before or after that event, I was accompanying her to the hospital at the time. And what we heard, I'm not quite sure whether we were being shot at or there were other targets, but what we heard was the whistling of the bullets, bullets whizzing by. And they went past very close to our heads. And as we took cover under a carriage and we waited for a good opportunity to get out, we did not take that road but we then used a path along -- on the hill. Later on, I could see these were some positions towards the hospital. And we turned and -- and I turned and I could see that from the upper floors of the -- of the skyscraper that was on Grbavica, between this bridge --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you please point to the map on your right rather than the map on the screen because then we can all see what it is you're pointing at.

utterances.speaker: MENSUR JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is Grbavica. This is the entire area of Grbavica, Grbavica I and Grbavica II. And in this area up to the Miljacka River, there are four skyscrapers; and the tops of these skyscrapers, from those tops, it is possible to see them from these positions, across the barracks here and the railway station, because the railway station is a little lower down. And then this area is the area of the former Marsal Tito barracks, and they are also a little lower, so it is possible to see the tops of these four skyscrapers. They had about 20 floors in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And what colour were those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, we are at a quarter to 2.00, if you would perhaps finish this part, and then find a suitable moment to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If it's convenient to you, Mr. President, it might be preferable if I was to stop at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Jusic, we'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this courtroom, and we'll adjourn until then. Tomorrow the examination by counsel for the Prosecution will continue, and then presumably you will be examined by counsel for the Defence. And if there are any additional questions to be put to you by the Judges, that will happen also. So we'll then adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 7th day of February 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 25
